items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: Alan Kaplan’s another trombone player that used to play golf with Carl, and the three of us would go out and play

ctx.x: Yeah. And four hours a day and then you’ve got to wait ‘til the next day to do so. That’s a lot of time to fill in. Yeah.

And then the next day there may not be work. You know sometimes you have a great week where you’re working a lot and bringing in a lot of money. The next week maybe one or two sessions and that’s it. And you know people just don’t know what to do with themselves sometimes. Some love playing golf like Carl Saunders, the trumpet player, really a great player. He was a great golfer. We’d go out and play golf. Alan Kaplan’s another trombone player that used to play golf with Carl, and the three of us would go out and…

I see. I wanted to wrap up just with an observation that I’ve been noticing and that is what used to be our word, and I’m speaking of “gig” — has now become usurped in a number of ways. I remember hearing DJs start talking about, “I have a gig tomorrow.” And I remember being like don’t say that, you don’t have a gig. And now we have the gig economy which further usurps our own word.
